messages:
erin: FYI, noticed p99 jump on streaming chat after kernel rollout v2.4. Rolling window: p95 ~120ms -> 150ms, p99 320ms -> 620ms.

sam: saw it. Is this only streaming? non-streaming completions look stable from dashboards.

marta: looks correlated with batcher settings. We increased default batch target from 4->8 in the rollout.

erin: Correct. Hypothesis: larger batches improve throughput but amplify tail because of head-of-line when small token streams wait for batch fill.

jason: Profiler traces attached from perf-bot: shows spikes in `kv_merge` and `cudaMemcpy` on p99.

perf-bot: trace-482: aggregated flame for 173 requests (link: https://perf/reports/trace-482) :link: :mag_right:

sam: Two things I noticed in the traces: kernel selection flips between `fused_attn_v2` and `generic_attn` for short sequences, causing extra kernel launch overhead for streaming tokens. Kernel warmup + launch jitter shows up on tails.

marta: Also KV cache behavior: streaming has high prefix reuse, but when the batcher groups heterogeneous contexts the `kv_merge` code does an extra memcpy per slot -> big tail costs on p99.

erin: Quick numbers from experiment A (same instance type, same load shape):
```
mb_target=1 -> throughput 120 req/s, p95 110ms, p99 260ms
mb_target=4 -> throughput 420 req/s, p95 130ms, p99 480ms
mb_target=8 -> throughput 700 req/s, p95 150ms, p99 620ms
```
Tradeoff is clear.

jason: For non-streaming completions with the same QPS, mb_target=8 gave the best cost/latency tradeoff (p99 ~300ms) because full sequences let the fused kernels amortize overhead.

sam: So action: config should be workload-aware. If request metadata says `stream: true` prefer small target (1-2) + immediate dispatch; if not streaming then allow larger targets to maximize throughput.

marta: Implementation idea: add `dispatch_mode` hint on route and an adaptive policy that measures per-route p99 and toggles `batch_target`. Also tune `kv_merge_threshold` to switch to in-place merge for common-prefix workloads to avoid big memcopies.

erin: Agreed. Concrete next steps:
1) rollback default mb_target for streaming pool to 2 in prod config and monitor.
2) add kernel selection logging (emit which kernel chosen per request) for 24h.
3) run controlled A/B with perf-bot traces and compare p50/p95/p99 and GPU utilization.

deploy-bot: Roll request created: `roll/1743212400` -> rollback default batch target for streaming pools to 2. :rocket:

sam: I'll add an eval job to run for 24h and collect p50/p95/p99, cost-per-token, and KV memcpy time.

marta: Also propose an emergency cutoff: if p99 > 2x baseline for streaming pool, auto-fallback to single-request dispatch for that pool until engineers triage.

erin: Perfect. Thanks team :thumbsup:
